title: Hamadab
description: Hamadab is an important archaeological site of the middle Nile River valley. It is the site of a ruined Kushite city located in what is now Sudan. The settlement was established by the third century BCE and remained active until the fourth century CE.

title: Pian della Conserva
description: An Etruscan necropolis located 5 km from Tolfa with tombs stretching from the Orientalizing period to the later Hellenistic.

title: Broglio di Trebisacce
description: Broglio di Trebisacce is the site of a protohistoric settlement located on the plain of Sibari not far from the Calabrian coast. Discovered in 1978, the site was excavsed by Renato Peroni from 1979 to 1985.

title: Giricano
description: Modern Giricano, site of the ancient Dunnu-ša-Uzībiis, is located in the Upper Tigris region of south-eastern Turkey, in the province of Diyarbakir, about 11 km southeast of modern Bismil, ca. 5 km northwest of Ziyaret Tepe, on the north bank of the Tigris River.

title: Tell Sabi Abyad
description: Tell Sabi Abyad is located in the Balih River Valley, in northern Syria. The ancient name of the site is not yet known.

title: Tagliata Etrusca
description: A rock-cut canal located at the port of ancient Cosa.

title: Karahan Tepe
description: Karahan Tepe is an archaeological site covering some 10 hectares located in Turkey's Şanlıurfa Province. More than 250 t-shaped monuments have been discovered at the site which is associated with the so-called Tepeler cultures. Karahan Tepe lies within the environs of Gôbekli Tepe and may pre-date that site.

title: Gladiatorial School
description: The gladiatorial school of Carnuntum was located to the west of the amphitheater.

title: Roman amphitheater at Nuceria (Alfaterna)

title: Greek Theater

title: Cave 13 at Udayagiri

title: Arzhan-1

title: Gre Virike Mound

title: Acumincum
description: Acumincum (modern Stari Slankamen in Serbia) was a settlement of the Scordisci that was later conquered by the Romans. During the Flavian period, the Cohors I Britannica equitata and II Adjutrix were based there.

title: Ad Fines
description: A Roman road station attested in ancient sources, possibly to be identified with modern Kuršumlija in Serbia.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 21 D6 Ad Fines

title: Zăvoi Roman Camp
description: A Roman camp located in the middle of the modern village of Zăvoi in Romania. The site may be associated with a road station known as Acmonia/Augmonia/Agnavi(a)e in ancient sources.

title: Cairn de Barnénez
description: A megalithic monument of the Neolithic period (ca. 4500 BCE) located near Plouezoc'h, on the Kernéléhen peninsula, in northern Finistère, Brittany

title: Fosso del Manganello
description: The stream known as the Fosso del Manganello is a stream that delimits the northern part of the tuff plateau upon which the Etruscan metropolis of Caere developed.

title: Martini-Marescotti Tomb
description: The so-called Martini-Marescotti Tomb is an Etruscan tomb located in the Monte Abatone necropolis of ancient Caere. The tomb was built in the late sixth or early fifth century BCE and is composed of a dromos and three funereal chambers covered by a tumulus. The tomb contained a substantial funereal deposit that included painted Attic wares.

title: Monte Torre Maggiore
description: An Italic temple complex in Umbria of the first millennium B.C. that includes the so-called "Ara maior".

title: Girsu Bridge
description: The archaeological site of the Girsu Bridge, located in modern Iraq's Dhi Qar governorate, was identified in 1920 and has been dated to the third millennium BCE.

title: Gutium
description: Gutium is a designation appearing in cuneiform texts of the third, second, and first millennia B.C. for the land of the Gutians (Akkadian Gutî or Qutî), a people responsible for bringing an end to the Akkadian empire. In first millennium B.C. sources, the name is used as an archaic designation for the region northeast of Babylonia, near and in the Zagros Mountains.

title: Tomb of Thutmes I and Hatshepsut (KV20)
description: KV20 may be the earliest tomb cut in the Valley of the Kings. It was first the tomb of Thutmose I, although he was later re-interred in KV38. KV20 was adapted to accommodate both her and her father.

title: Ancient harbour (submerged) at Aegina
description: Archaeological remains of Aegina's military harbor.

title: Ancient sanctuary at Marion
description: An Iron Age sanctuary located at Peristeries in Polis Chrysochous, Cyprus, dedicated to the female goddess of Cyprus that was in use for half a millennium, from ca. 950 to ca. 450 BCE.

title: Sant'Andrea Catabarbara
description: Sant'Andrea Catabarbara was a church located in Rome; it was dedicated to Saint Andrew. It likely succeeds the fourth-century CE civil basilica known as the Basilica of Iunius Bassus, via the patronage of the Goth general Valila. Its remains were demolished in 1930 and its site is now occupied by the Pontifical Oriental Institute on Via Napoleone III, in the Esquilino district.

title: Turlu Höyük
description: Tell Turlu (Turlu Höyük) is ca. 7 km northwest of Nizip (Gaziantep Province, Turkey), near the modern village Turlu. In 2003, a basalt stele of the Assyrian official Bēl-iddin (reign of Sargon II; r. 721–705 BC) was discovered there. The ancient name of this large site, which was occupied in the Neolithic Period, is not known.

title: Castellaccio Europarco
description: A villa and a number of burials located along the Via Laurentina, dating from the fourth century BC to the second century AD.

title: Torre Dell'Angelo
description: A Roman columbarium tomb located on the Via Latina.

description: A river in central Morocco that flows from the eastern High Atlas to the Atlantic Ocean.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 1a C2 Fut/ Quosenum?/ Kousa? fl.

description: Treasury of Thutmose I at Karnak from the beginning of the New Kingdom.

description: Tor Tignosa, mapped and listed in the 17th century Catasto Alessandrino as a landed estate, is a ruined stone structure located some 8 km northeast of Lavinium. description: Once known as İririn or Érérin and now known as Dağönü, this modern Turkish village located in the Van Province of eastern Turkey at the eastern coast of Lake Van lies ca. 10 km north of Ayanis. title: ad Capita bubula
description: The toponym "ad Capita bubula" is attested in Suetonius and refers to a place located at the northeast corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome near the Curiae Veteres. Here, there was a domus of one Caius Octavius, a Roman politician who was the biological father of Octavian. It is possible that Octavian was born in this domus, and the sources suggest that the location was later commemorated with the construction of a shrine (sacrarium) and, eventually, a temple.

title: Hyctanis (river)

title: Imgur-Enlil
description: The great, inner wall of Babylon was called by the ceremonial Akkadian name Imgur-Enlil, which means "The God Enlil Showed Favor." According to the text Tintir = Babylon, Imgur-Enlil had eight city gates, four on the eastern side of the Euphrates and four on the western side of the river. The Assyrian kings Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal and the Babylonian kings Nabopolassar, Nebuchadnezzar II, and Nebonidus all undertook construction on Babylon’s great wall. Imgur-Enlil is one of the seven wonders of the ancient according to some classical sources.

title: Sumer
description: Sumer (Akkadian Šumeru; Sumerian Kiengir) is the name of a historical region of southern Mesopotamia, now modern-day southern Iraq. It is home to one of the world’s earliest civilizations and one of the places where writing was first developed. Eridu, Girsu, Lagash, Shuruppak, Umma, Ur, and Uruk are among its most well-known urban centers.

title: Perorsi

title: Euganeae gentes
description: Euganeae gentes describes an ancient confederation of pre-Roman peoples dwelling in northeast Italy, between the Adriatic Sea and the Alps. The exact nature of this group is difficult to define. Drawing upon Cato the Elder, Pliny the Elder asserts that the Euganeae gentes were divided into three groups: the Stoeni, the Triumpilini, and the Camuni.

title: Souk el Arba
description: A Roman camp with baths and associated settlement were identified at modern Souk El Arbaa in Morocco in the late 19th and 20th centuries on high ground occupied by a qubba called "Sidi Aïssa". title: Atrium Libertatis

description: A small shrine with an altar built before 480 BC on the Acropolis of Athens. The northern colonnade of the Parthenon was built around this shrine, preserving it in situ. It is unknown what cult it housed.

title: Elginhaugh Roman fort
description: Site of the most completely excavated timber-built auxiliary fort (with annexe) in the Roman Empire, situated in present-day Midlothian, Scotland. Roman occupation was short-lived, having been established in the early 70s CE and abandoned in or shortly after 86. Now completely built over by the Royal Bank of Scotland Data Centre.

title: Penkalas Bridge

title: Regio XIV (Transtiberim)
description: The fourteenth regio of imperial Rome was created by the Augustan administrative reform of 7 BCE. This region contained, in addition to the named monuments, the statio of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, 78 shrines (aediculae), 150 townhouses, 22 warehouses (horrea), 86 bathhouses, and 180 fountains. At the beginning of the fifth century, the Regio was subdivided into 78 districts or vici and 4,405 insulae.

description: Gors Fawr Stone Circle is located in Mynachlog-Ddu, Pembrokeshire, Wales, United Kingdom.

description: A settlement and cemetery in use from ca. 8000 BCE into the first millennium.

title: Aliphera sanctuary
description: Pausanias observed sanctuaries of both Asclepius and Athena at Aliphera, as well as an altar of Zeus Lecheates.

title: Oluz Höyük
description: Mound site in Amasya province, Turkey. First inhabited in the Early Bronze Age (ca. 4500 BCE), the site was abandoned sometime during the Hittite Period (15th-13th centuries BCE). It was briefly resettled during the Iron Age-Hellenistic period (8th-1st centuries BCE).

title: Santuario di Santa Maria Regina di Anglona
description: A Marian sanctuary located on the hill of Anglona in the province of Matera, Italy, that originates in the eleventh century.

title: Karabel Reliefs
description: A monument consisting of multiple Hittite rock reliefs with Luwian inscriptions, probably dating to the 13th century BCE, located in the Karabel pass on the southern slopes of Mount Nif in Turkey's Izmir province. Most of the reliefs and inscriptions known to western scholars from the 19th and 20th centuries have been lost to road construction and vandalism.

title: Düzceli
description: The findspot of an Urartian inscription.

title: Oedipodia
description: A spring in Boeotia.

title: Roman bridge at Valeriana
description: A bridge constructed across the Danube at the Roman fort of Valeriana.

title: Kharaneh IV
description: Kharaneh IV is an archaeological site located in Jordan. This site has produced evidence of human occupation during the Late Pleistocene, ca. 18,900 to 16,600 BCE.

title: Aspronisi
description: A volcanic island that formed on the southwestern edge of the Santorini archipelago following a major volcanic eruption that occurred ca. 1625 BC.

title: Tobillas
description: A village located in the valley of the Omecillo River, a tributary of the Ebro. Tobillas has been the focus of a case study interested in the processes of village formation from both archaeological and historical perspectives.

title: Osteria Cessati Spiriti
description: In the Notizie degli Scavi di Antichità for 1884, R. Lanciani reports the find of a monolithic, anepigraphic Roman sarcophagus at the Osteria Cessati Spiriti. The sarcophagus had been discovered in a pozzolana quarry and relocated to the grounds of the osteria. Brickstamps dating to 123 CE were reportedly observed at its reputed findspot.

title: Santuario di Fondo Patturelli
description: A Samnite sanctuary of ancient Capua that was initially discovered in 1845. Active from the sixth century B.C. until the first century B.C., the Santuario di Fondo Patturelli is noted for its architectural terracotta as well as for the presence of a sacred maternal cult.

title: Samnite House
description: The so-called "Samnite House" is a domus in Herculaneum that originally dates to the second century B.C., making it one of the oldest buildings discovered at the site.

title: Manor House Roman villa
description: The site of a Roman corridor villa with a separate bathhouse. Three phases dating from the late first century AD into the fourth century. It possibly forms part of a complex with the villa uncovered ca. 250 meters to the south and east.

title: Amathus necropolis
description: The necropolis of Amathus on Cyprus.

title: Khirbat Iskandar
description: A fortified site on the banks of the Wadi al-Wala in Jordan inhabited in the Early Bronze IV period.

title: Zingsheim
description: A Gallo-Roman temple of the Matronae Aufaniae.

title: Urartu
description: An eastern Anatolian kingdom on the eastern shore of Lake Van. Originating from a regional collection of principalities first mentioned in the 13th century BCE, it had become a single political entity by the 9th century BCE. Urartu was a powerful rival to the Neo-Assyrian Empire. It ceased to exist sometime in the late 7th or early 6th century BCE.

title: Ponte Scotonico
description: An ancient Roman bridge located along the Via Valeria near Roviano, Italy.

title: Tartas-1
description: Burial site near the banks of the Tartas River in Western Siberia containing over 400 burials, mostly associated with the Krotovo (Chernoozero) and Andronovo (Fedorovo) cultures and dated to the 3rd-2nd millennia BCE

title: Puskan Castle
description: Sassanid fort located about 3.5km south of the Iranian town Puskan. The fort is square shaped with a round tower at each corner.

title: Altheim-Weirading villa rustica
description: A Roman "villa rustica" occupied from ca. 80 - 240 CE, located in the Innviertel region, northeast of the Austrian town of Altheim, village of Weirading (Kiriberg district). This is one of three such sites in the general vicinity of Altheim.

title: Palaikastro, Crete
description: Palaikastro, located in eastern Crete, was an important trading center in antiquity, from the Bronze Age going forward.

title: Agelastos Petra
description: A mythic rock formation at Eleusis where Demeter searched for Persephone.

title: Domus dei Coiedii
description: The so-called Domus dei Coiedii is a domus located at Suasa. It dates to the first century B.C.

title: Tell Aḥmad al-Ḥattū
description: Early dynastic necropolis in southern Mesopotamia. The site was inundated by the creation of Lake Hamrin in 1981.

title: Kallipatrai
description: A chorion (probably a small village, farm or estate), attested only in a single inscription, and probably located somewhere south of the site of Larisa in Aiolis.

title: Emašdari
description: The temple of the goddess Ištar of Agade at Babylon. The Sumerian ceremonial name Emašdari means "House of Animal Offerings." The Neo-Babylonian king Nabonidus rebuilt/renovated it.

title: Emeslam
description: The temple of the god Nergal at Cutha. The Sumerian ceremonial name Emeslam means "House, Warrior of the Netherworld."

title: Bēlet-ilī Gate
description: The Bēlet-ilī Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Bēlet-ilī-murappišat-talittīšu ("The Goddess Bēlet-ilī Is the One Who Increases Its (Animals’) Offspring"), is the eighth of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the second of the south-facing entrances to the city, but its precise location remains unknown.

title: Ea Gate
description: The Ea Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Ea-muštēšir-nagbīšu ("The God Ea Is the One Who Keeps Its Spring(s) in Good Order"), is the seventh of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the first of the south-facing entrances to the city, but its precise location remains unknown.

title: Shepherds' Field
description: A chapel located in the Palestinian village of Beit Sahour that is believed to be the site of the annunciation of Jesus Christ's birth to the shepherds. A Christian monastery was founded on the site in the early fifth century.

title: Solomon's Pools
description: The so-called "Solomon's Pools" are three ancient reservoirs located in the south-central West Bank, approximately 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) southwest of Bethlehem. They date to the early Roman period.

title: Asklepieion at Eleusis
description: A sanctuary of Asklepios at Eleusis, active from the late 5th century BC until the 3rd century AD, known from inscriptions found in a field 1.5 km north of the sanctuary of Demeter and Kore on the bank of the Kephisos River in the 1890s. The site has never been archaeologically explored and the exact location is now unknown.

title: Al-'Assāsīf
description: Necropolis on the West Bank of the Nile near Thebes containing tombs from the 18th, 25th, and 26th dynasties.

title: Daskalio
description: An island of the Cyclades that is now uninhabited. The Cambridge Keros Project identified a large Bronze Age settlement on the island.

title: Monte di Terra tomb
description: A monumental Roman tomb located at the ninth mile of the Via Appia, the Monte di Terra tomb rests on a quadrangular podium in peperino stone that supports a circular concrete core and an earthen tumulus.

title: Roman amphitheater of Virunum
description: The Virunum Roman amphitheater is located in Maria Saal, Austria.

title: Chelmos Castle
description: The Kastro Chelmou was a medieval castle, built probably in the 13th century of the modern era inside the ancient Athenaion fortress in Arcadia. It is located on the hill of Agios Konstantinos, southeast of the modern town of Skortsino.

title: Temple of Al-Lat at Palmyra
description: A temple sacred to the goddess Al-Lat in Palmyra. The earliest shrine on the site was constructed in the mid-first century BCE, and was greatly expanded during the second century CE. The temple was closed and its altar destroyed during the 380s CE.

title: Ponte Barucelli
description: A Roman aqueduct bridge located in the comune of Gallicano nel Lazio (Rome, Italy). It was once part of the Aqua Claudia.

title: Savignano sul Rubicone Roman bridge
description: A Roman bridge on the Rubicon at Savignano sul Rubicone.

title: Ishān Miziyād
description: Large mound north of Kish, Akkadian settlement and find place for cuneiform inscriptions.

title: Spathari (quarry)
description: A limestone quarry located just south of the modern Acarnanian village of Lepenou with clear evidence of having been used as a source for the construction of the temple of Zeus and other monuments at nearby ancient Stratos.

title: Fundus Flaminianus

description: An ancient river of north Africa, placed by the Ravenna Geographer between the Isaris (modern Oued Isser) and the Ligar (perhaps the Siga). Modern identification of the Nigrensis is uncertain: the modern Oued Amieur, Salsaf, Sikkak, and Tafna are all candidates.

title: Greek theater, Monte Iato
description: The Greek theater of Monte Iato was built in the fourth century BCE at a site already inhabited by the Elymians. The theater complex had a long life, used for the same purpose in the Roman period and repurposed as a domestic space by Arab occupiers in the seventh century.

title: Yüceören necropolis
description: Burial ground near Yüceören Hill in Cilicia containing tombs from the Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine periods.

title: Džanfida
description: Džanfida is a village located in the Armavir province of southwestern Armenia, ca. 9 km south of Sardarabat. Here a stone block with an inscription of Sarduri II (8th century BCE) was found which curses anyone who dares to damage or destroy his fortress or inscription.

title: Phylakopi
description: A major Bronze Age settlement on Melos with evidence for continuous occupation from the third millennium BC until the twelfth century BC, Phylakopi provides important information about the Cycladic civilization.

title: Bingöl Dağ (epigraphic findspot)
description: Find spot for a Urartian stele.

title: Sanctuary of Artemis Limnatis at Messene
description: A sanctuary on the slopes of Mount Ithome and within the city walls of ancient Messene in the Peloponnese. The sanctuary developed beginning in the 4th-3rd centuries BCE.

title: Ezida
description: One of the temples in the citadel of Nineveh that was dedicated to Nabû, the god of scribes; it is located north of the temple of the goddess Ištar (Emašmaš). The Sumerian ceremonial name Ezida means "True House."

title: Castle an Dinas
description: Castle an Dinas is an Iron Age hillfort near St. Columb Major in Cornwall, United Kingdom, built during the third and second centuries BC.

description: Mythological river of the Greek Underworld

title: Osmanthorpe Roman vexillation fortress
description: The remains of Osmanthorpe Roman vexillation fortress are situated on a hilltop in the valley of the River Greet.

title: Grotta delle Veneri
description: In the Grotta delle Veneri, human occupation can be documented from the Mousterian Age until the Neolithic and Bronze Ages.

title: Tall Yalkhī
description: Mound and find place for cuneiform inscription, partly submerged.

title: Yazılıtaş
description: Find place for cuneiform inscription.

title: Temple of Hibis
description: A large temple located in the Kharga Oasis that is dated to the Saite-Persian period.

title: Māri
description: Mari (Tell Hariri) was an ancient Semitic city that flourished as a trade center and hegemonic state between 2900 BC until 1759 BC. The site was submitted as a tentative candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1999.

title: Unnamed aqueduct (near Siga)
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 29 D1 unnamed aqueduct (near Siga)

title: Unnamed aqueduct (near Mina)
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 29 F1 unnamed aqueduct (near Mina)

title: Pons Sublicius
description: The Pons Sublicius is traditionally held to be the earliest Roman bridge across the river Tiber. The textual tradition assigns its construction to the king Ancus Marcius in 642 B.C. It crossed the Tiber River near the Forum Boarium just downstream from Tiber Island.

title: Castle of Serravalle
description: The Castle of Serravalle is a twelfth century castle located in Bosa, province of Oristano, Sardinia. It is connected with the Tuscan Malaspina family.

title: Ness of Brodgar
description: Ness of Brodgar is an archaeological site near Loch of Harray, Orkney. The site covers 2.5 hectares.

title: Lisinae
description: Lisinae was an ancient town of Histiaeotis in Thessaly.

title: Kom Firin
description: Egyptian settlement located in the western half of the Nile Delta.

title: Nesiotic League (Second)
description: A re-establishment of the first Nesiotic League, the second Nesiotic League was founded by Rhodes in in c.  200 BCE and was dissolved in c. 167 BCE.

title: Nesiotic League (First)
description: The Nesiotic league (the League of the Islanders) was a federal organization of Greek poleis in the Cyclades islands, organized in ca.  314/3 BCE under the direction of Antigonus Monophthalmus. Control passed to the Ptolemies ca. 287 BCE; the league eventually dissolved in the mid-3rd century BCE.

title: al-Jumayil
description: An archaeological site of Byzantine and possibly earlier date located at the modern town of al-Jumayil in Jordan. It may be identifiable as the biblical site of Beth Gamul.

title: Pieve a Bozzone
description: The ruins of an ancient Roman villa were discovered in the Italian comune of Pieve a Bozzone (Siena) in 2023.

title: Coriaria Septimiana
description: A place included the Regionary Catalogues for Rome's Regio XIV, Coriaria Septimiana refers to tanneries in the Transtiberim. On the basis of epigraphic evidence, the place listed in the Notitia is associated with a small tanning facility on the site of the paleochristian church of Saint Cecilia in Trastevere.

title: Mausoleo della Conocchia
description: A Roman mausoleum dating most likely to the second century.

title: Alburnus Maior
description: A settlement and gold mining complex at modern Roşia Montană in Romania. The Roșia Montană Mining Landscape was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021.

title: Indus Delta
description: The delta of the Indus river.

title: Absheron (peninsula)
description: A peninsula in the South Caucasus, extending approximately 60 km into the Caspian Sea.

title: Philippaioi
description: A Hellenistic fortified site located southwest of modern Philippaioi in the municipal territory of Grevena in Greece's decentralized administration of Epirus and Western Macedonia

title: Mausoleum Augusti
description: A monumental tomb built in the Campus Martius at Rome by Augustus and dedicated in 28 B.C. The mausoleum served as a family tomb for the Iulio-Claudians.
names_attested_other: Mausoleo di Augusto@it|τὸ Μαυσώλειον@grc|Mausoleum des Augustus@de

title: New Palace at Assur
description: The Middle Assyrian king Tukultī-Ninurta I (1233–1197 BC) built himself a new royal residence at Assur. That palace, which went by the Sumerian name Elugalumunkurkurra (“House of the King, Lord of the Lands”), covered an area of about 27000 m². After Tukultī-Ninurta I’s reign, the so-called “New Palace” was no longer maintained and, thus, fell into ruins.

title: Catacombe San Marcellino e Pietro
description: The Catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter lies some 3 km southeast of Rome along the ancient Via Labicana. They date to the fourth century A.D.

title: Wall0045, Christian house church (Dura-Europos)
description: Wall portion on the north-facing exterior side of the baptismal font from the Baptistery, Christian House Church, Dura-Europos.

title: Arch of Septimius Severus
description: The Arch of Septimius Severus dates to 205.

title: Jrvezh
description: Village east of Yerevan in Armenia. The town, which has been settled since at least the 5th century CE, contains a 7th-century chapel.

title: Unnamed naiskos tomb, Fondo Pacifico
description: An unnamed naiskos tomb located in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

title: Nēmed-Marduk
description: The outer city wall of Nippur according to the so-called "Kuyunjik Ziqqurrat List" (7th century B.C.). Its Akkadian ceremonial name means "Bulwark of the God Marduk".

title: Hambledon Hill
description: Hambledon Hill is a prehistoric hill fort in Dorset, England, with occupation beginning in the Neolithic period.

title: Basilica of Thyrsos
description: A fifth or sixth century AD (Early Christian) triple-aisled basilica including mosaic floors.

title: Tumulus of Glimes
description: A Gallo-Roman tumulus located near Incourt, Belgium.

title: Trou de Billemont Tumulus
description: The Trou de Billemont Tumulus is a second century AD Gallo-Roman tumulus in Belgium.

title: Heroön
description: The so-called Heroön at Sagalassos dominates the Upper Agora in the northwest sector of the city.

title: Dema Tower
description: A round defensive tower located to the east of the Dema Wall in Attica.

title: Cluster of 9 mausolea
description: South of modern Kherba Sidi el Ahmar in Algeria (BAtlas 29 G1 unlabeled)

title: Sidi Moussa
description: A modern village located at the western end of the municipal territory of Nador in Algeria's Tipaza province. According to Anselmino, this village, which was built to house the displaced population of Chénoua during the Algerian War of Independence in the mid-20th century, probably covers the site of an ancient settlement and associated necropolis.

title: Nazzano Romano
description: Nazzano Romano was the site of an Etruscan settlement covering some 7 hectares and dating between the eighth and fifth centuries B.C.

title: Temple of Artemis Azzanathkona Phase 1 (Dura-Europos)
description: Archaeological phase (c. 13-160 CE) of the Temple at Dura-Europos dedicated to Artemis Azzanathkona, probably the tutelary deity of the Euphrates island settlement Anath.

title: Tino (island)
description: An island in the Ligurian Sea designated as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Tino is connected with the life of the seventh-century AD Christian Saint Venerius.

title: Aletrinates
description: The inhabitants of Alētrium.

title: Vigna Parrocchiale archaeological area
description: A complex of civic and sacred buildings in the urban area of ancient Caere, including the so-called "elliptical building".

title: Ferrone Necropolis
description: An Etruscan necropolis located on a tufaceous plateau overlooking the valley of the Fosso della Lenta. The tombs in the necropolis date between the seventh and fifth centuries BCE.

title: Arco del Sacramento
description: A Roman arch of the second century A.D. that faced on to the forum of Beneventum.

title: Abara
description: A place included in the Peutinger map.

title: Masqaṭ
description: A place from the TAVO Index

title: Elugalgalgasisa
description: The ziggurat of the god Sîn at Ur. The Sumerian ceremonial name Elugalgalgasisa means "House of the King who Lets Counsel Flourish". The platform temple was originally built during the Early Bronze Age and was then restored in the sixth century B.C. by King Nabonidus.

title: Chillon
description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Ciudad Real that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today knowh as Chillón.

title: Almaden
description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Ciudad Real that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today known as Almadén.

title: Hattusa
description: The Late Bronze Age capital of the Hittite empire (near modern Boğazkale in Turkey). The site was enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

title: Temple G at Selinus
description: Remains of an octastyle Doric temple begun in the sixth century B.C. but left unfinished.

title: Redones
description: A Celtic tribe living in the area of modern Brittany counted among the civitates maritimae or Aremorica.

title: Nuraghe Mannu (Doragli)

title: Horoztepe Hellenistic Fortification
description: Olshausen describes at Horoztepe (Berg) the remains of a fortified settlement (Burg-ruinen) with Hellenistic stairways, cisterns, and rock tombs, but walls of a "later date". Horoztepe, located at modern Bergaa in Turkey's Tokat province, is best known as the site of a Bronze Age settlement and associated cemetery of the Hatti culture. Only cursory publications of the mid-20th-century excavations have appeared; none mention a later fortification, and none are visible in modern, publicly available aerial/satellite imagery.

title: Khorsabad Residence J
description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) had several royal residences constructed in the citadel of his new capital, Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad). Residence J, which has constructed on the western side of the citadel, is presumed to have been for one of the highest officials of the Assyrian Empire. Since no inscriptions were discovered in the ruins of the building, the owner/principal occupant of the this Assyrian palace is not known.

title: Pagania Sanctuary (Aigies, Laconia)

title: Mané-Vechen, Plouhinec
description: A Gallo-Roman villa excavated in 1970-1971. A possible fanum was identified 50 meters to the northwest of the villa.

title: Hovhannavank
description: Medieval Armenian monastery in the village of Ohanavan, Aragatsotn Province, Armenia. The site originated as a single-nave church in the 4th century CE, was expanded in the 4th-5th centuries, and was substantially renovated in the 17th-18th centuries.

title: Anfiteatro di Bleso

title: Pont de Bornègre

title: Gallo-Roman settlement, locality of Courac
description: Near the locality of Courac, just north of modern Tresques, are the remains of a diffuse Gallo-Roman settlement occupied from the first to fourth centuries A.D.

title: Cercina (Etruria)
description: A now-unlocated place near Florentia in Etruria (Regio VII) known from epigraphic sources. Caius Caesar, the father of Iulius Caesar, helmed a veterans' colony there.

title: Karagündüz
description: Karagündüz (Armenian name: Charakonis) is a modern village on the eastern coast of Lake Erceç in southeastern Turkey. Here a stela with an inscription of the Urartian kings Išpuini (9th century BCE) and Minua (9th / 8th century BCE) was found which praises the victory over the cites Mešta, Qua, Šaritu, and Nigibi and the land Paršua and gives detailed information about the numbers of soldiers, spoils and deportees (CTU I A 3-9). Furthermore, a partially preserved stela authored by Minua, son of Išpuini, has been found alone (CTU I A 5-86).

title: Artemis Laphria Sanctuary (Kalydon)
description: This sanctuary is believed to have been active since at least the Geometric period, possibly on the site of a Mycenaean settlement. Ceramic evidence indicates continuous activity at least through the Roman period.

title: Roman theater at Verona
description: The Roman theater at Verona dates from the late first century B.C.

title: Rock Carvings in Tanum
description: The Rock Carvings in Tanum is a collection of petroglyphs located near Tanumshede, Bohuslän, Sweden. This heritage landscape is composed of at least 600 rock-cut panels covering an area of some 51 ha (126 acres). Many of the figural motifs are maritime in nature and pertain to the European Bronze Age.

title: So-called Central Church in Apollonia
description: A three-aisled basilical church, with an external apse, situated near the centre of the ancient settlement of Apollonia (Cyrenaica), about halfway between the East and West churches. The building has a narthex, a small western atrium and a range of added rooms along the north flank. The mosaics have been dated to around the sixth century AD, but the building seems to have been built in earlier times (possibly the fifth century AD).

title: Ponte delle Serretelle
description: The so-called Ponte delle Serretelle is an ancient arched bridge located southwest of Benevento, Italy. It lies between the Gran Potenza hill and the Serretelle stream. It may have once been located either at or near the point where the Serretelle and the Calor converged.

title: Ponte Apollosa
description: Ponte Apollosa, a bridge of the Via Appia that may have been restored by Septimius Severus in 198 CE.

title: Tomba delle Anatre
description: The Tomb of the Ducks at Veii is an early example of a painted Etruscan tomb. It dates to the second quarter of the seventh century BCE and was discovered in 1958 in the Riserva del Bagno necropolis.

title: Saint-Pierre-d'Aurillac
description: Remains of Gallo-Roman substructures that support the choir of the present church.

title: Temple of Veiovis
description: The Temple of Veiovis, also attested as Aedes Vediovis, was a temple of ancient Rome located on the Capitoline Hill in a location known as "inter duos lucos", which is interpreted to mean a saddle between the two summits of the hill. The remains of a temple podium were discovered beneath the northwest corner of the Palazzo Senatore in 1938-1939.

title: Tor di Mezzavia di Frascati
description: The Tor di Mezzavia is a Medieval tower located along the modern Via Tuscolana, marking the midway point between Rome and Frascati.

title: Pompeii II.3.7 garden entrance
description: Pompeii II, 3, 7 is a garden entrance linked to II, 3, 8 and II, 3,9. II, 3, 8 is identified as a workshop, either the Officina vasaria or caupona of Nicanor. This complex was positioned across the street from the Palaestra.

title: Mausoleum of Lucius Munatius Plancus

description: Remains of a Roman amphitheater at Chassenon.

title: Thrace/Skudra (satrapy)
description: A satrapy of the Achaemenid Persian empire established in Thrace in 513 BC by Darius I and Megabazus and abandoned in 479 BC following the failure of Xerxes' invasion of Greece. It was a minor satrapy, subordinate to the central main satrapy of Lydia.

title: San Saba, Rome
description: The Basilica of San Saba is located on the "Piccolo Aventino" in Rome. The basilica's origin is traced to 645 when fugitive monks from Mar Saba in Palestine traveled to Rome to attend the Lateran Council. They subsequently remained on the Aventine.

title: Ezida (Kalhu)
description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the god Nabû. Unlike most of the religious buildings constructed at Kalhu, the Ezida ("True House") was built in the southeast corner of the Citadel.

title: Hexamilion wall
description: The Hexamilion wall is an ancient defensive wall built across the Isthmus of Corinth that protected the only land route into the Peloponnese from mainland Greece.

title: Ménec alignments

title: Petit-Ménec alignments
description: An alignment of megaliths located east of Kerlescan.

title: Betitius Perpetuus Arzygius, Domus
description: A domus included in Regio III, the house of Betitius Perpetuus Arzygius was located on the Quirinal Hill close to the ara incendii Neroniani. Some of its remains have been documented beneath the present Palazzo delle Esposizioni.

title: Porticus Absidata
description: The Porticus Absidata was an exedra porticata that served as the northern apsidal entryway to the Forum of Nerva, also known as the Forum Transitorium.

title: Enamhe
description: The temple of the gods Adad and Apla-Adad at Anat (Anatho). The Sumerian ceremonial name Enamhe means "House of Plenty."

title: Beacon Hill Hillfort

title: Battlesbury Camp

title: Temple of Jupiter, Damascus
description: The Temple of Jupiter in Damascus was begun during the rule of Augustus and completed during the rule of Constantius II.

title: Nether Denton Roman fort
description: A Roman fort site at Nether Denton that was identified via cropmarks. The fort formed part of the Stanegate frontier system, and thus pre-dates Hadrian's Wall. It was abandoned ca. 122.

title: Boothby Roman fort
description: A Roman fortlet that was part of the Stanegate system, dating to the late first to second centuries.

title: Göbekli Tepe
description: The site of Göbekli Tepe, located in the Germuş mountains of south-eastern Anatolia, was the location of a Neolithic hilltop sanctuary. This sanctuary, thought to be a series of stone enclosures with T-shaped pillars carrying carving of wild animals, was built in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic and ranges in date from 9,600 to 8,200 B.C.

title: Roman villa at Maasbracht
description: A Roman villa near the modern village of Maasbracht, Limburg, Netherlands, famous for its murals. The earliest structures on the site are dated to the second century CE, and the villa was abandoned by the middle of the third century.

title: Civitavecchia di Arpino
description: The fortified acropolis of the ancient city of Arpinum.

title: Cadmea

title: tribus Teretina
description: Established in 299 B.C., the tribus Teretina was one of the later rural tribes of ancient Rome.

title: Kadembas/Katepants
description: Kadembas (Katepants) is a modern settlement in the Van Province in the Southeast of Turkey. Here several rock inscriptions of the Urartian king Minua (9th / 8th century BCE) were found which report the construction of the “Canal of Minua” which is still in use today. Furthermore a rock inscription of Tariria, wife of Minua, (9th / 8th century BCE) is located here which attributes a vineyard to her belongings.

title: Kalecik
description: Kalecik (formerly known as Aralesk or Lesk) is a modern village situated ca. 5 km north of Van Kalesi in southeast Turkey. In the village church, a re-used cylindrical stone (presumably a column base) with a building inscription of the Urartian king Išpuini, son of Sarduri I (ninth century BCE), was found. Furthermore, a re-used stone slab with an inscription of the Urartian king Argišti, son of Minua and grandson of Išpuini (eighth century BCE) has also been found here.

title: Spring at Amphiareion
description: The spring at the healing sanctuary at Amphiareion and a site of votive deposits in the form of coins. It still flows today.

title: House of the Tiles
description: The so-called "House of the Tiles" at Lerna belongs to the Korakou culture in the Early Helladic II period (ca. 2500–2300 BCE). It was a monumental two-story building (12 x 25 meters) and has been interpreted as either a "proto-palace" or administrative center.

title: Tell es-Samarat
description: A multi-period settlement site located in the Jericho Governorate, West Bank.

title: St. Hilarion Castle
description: A Byzantine castle in Cyprus likely built in the late eleventh century. The site was a holiday retreat for Cyprus's Frankish rulers, and the Venetians destroyed it in the fourteenth century.

title: Tall-i-Gap
description: Site in Southern Iran, just north of the village Tajabad, with seven tells from a time-frame equivalent with the Ubaid to early-Uruk periods.

title: Assur Archive 25
description: In the northern corner, along the northwest town wall of Assur (bD5I, bC/D5II, bC5III), researchers unearthed Houses 67–68 with an archive belonging to a family with the title ḫunduraya, a gentilic meaning "from Ḫundur". Another archive belonging to a related family of ḫunduraya was found nearby (Assur Archive 24). In House 67 and 68, about 48 clay tablets and fragments were found. The tablets mostly date to the second half of the 7th century BC. The archive consists of loans, mostly concerning silver, work contracts, purchase documents and a juridical settlement.

title: Peiraic Gate
description: A gate in the Themistoklean Walls of Athens, through which the road to Peiraeus ran.

title: Egalgabarinutukua
description: The palace of the eighth-century-BC Assyrian Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) at Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), Egalgabarinutukua ("Palace That Has No Equal"), was constructed between 717 BC and 706 BC. This royal residence was constructed on a high, mud-brick terrace located within the city’s citadel, which was located against the northwestern stretch of the city wall. This large, ornately-decorated palace complex consisted of over two hundred rooms (including chapels to the deities Ea, Sîn, Ningal, Adad, Šamaš, and Ninurta) and courtyards, as well as a ziggurat.

title: Porticus Octaviae
description: A porticus in the area of the Circus Flaminius, the Porticus Octaviae was dedicated by Augustus sometime after 27 B.C. in honor of his sister, Octavia Minor. The porticus replaced the Porticus Metelli. It was restored twice after major urban fires in A.D. 80 and 203.

title: Sra Ghundai, Ghazni
description: Remains of a walled ancient city in the Ghazni province of Afghanistan. Its remains date to various periods according to W. Ball (1982): Late Sassanian and Turki Shahi (sixth–ninth century AD) and Early Islamic (tenth -twelfth century).

title: Pust-i Gau
description: A large, multi-period site in modern Afghanistan. One of its key feature is a large, fortified enclosure with 48 towers.

title: Burgast
description: Area in the Altai region of extreme western Mongolia containing a number of burials and other structures from the Bronze Age (Bulan-Kobin Culture), Turkic, and Medieval periods.

title: Via Campana?
description: A road located on the right bank of the Tiber River leading to the Campus Salinarum romanarum and sharing the first part of its course with the Via Portuensis.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 43 B2 Via Campana?

title: Acarnanian League
description: The Acarnanian League was a tribal confederation of the Acarnanians that later transformed into a league by the 5th century BCE. The league was incorporated into the Roman province of Achaea following the battle of Actium in 31 BCE.

title: Formina Roman aqueduct
description: The Formina Roman aqueduct provided water to the ancient city of Narnia. It originally dates to the first century CE. After antiquity, the first notice of it is recorded in 1371.

title: Terme della Trinacria
description: The so-called Terme della Trinacria in Regio III of Ostia Antica were built in the Hadrianic period at the same time as the Temple of Serapis (III,XVII,4). The modern toponym is derived from a triskelion included in a mosaic decoration.

title: Serapeum
description: The Serapeum in Ostia's Regio III was built between 123 and 126 CE thanks to private patronage.

title: Minoan Palatial Center (Knossos)
description: An extensive, multi-period Bronze Age palace complex, located south of modern Heraklion in central Crete.

title: Hazī
description: A town presumably located in or near the kingdom of Suhu, in the middle Euphrates region.

title: Camp of Diocletian at Palmyra
description: Camp of Diocletian in the Ancient City of Palmyra. Coordinates determined by eye in Google Earth in November 2012, following description in UNESCO World Heritage List.

title: Sanctuary at Leben
description: Leben is known for a sanctuary of Asklepios dating to the first and second centuries CE.

title: Lobera
description: A Spanish village located in the northwest of the province of Jaén, between Jaén and Córdoba, that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as Lopera.

title: Clepsydra of the Oropos Amphiareion
description: The Oropos Amphiareion clepsydra is a hydraulic inflow clock serving the Sanctuary of Amphiaraus. Situated on the southeast bank of the sacred spring of Amphiaraus, this inflow hydraulic clock dates to the 4th century BCE.

title: Ponte del Diavolo
description: A bridge in the territory of Blera known as the "Devil's Bridge".

title: Can Blai
description: A Late Roman fortlet on the island of Formentera.

title: Pozzuolo necropolis
description: A necropolis of Etruscan Veii.

title: Ocazanes (river)
description: A river that was a tributary of the Cyrus.

title: Oeandenses
description: An ancient people of Galatia.

title: Ahramat Branch
description: An ancient, now-vanished, branch of the Nile River. Geophysical research has demonstrated that the Ahramat Branch, no longer visible to the naked eye, was located west of the main Nile River channel and flowed from south of Lisht to the area of the Giza Plateau area. This channel would have bordered on the complexes of more than 30 ancient pyramids ranging in date from the Old Kingdom to Second Intermediate Period (2686−1649 BCE).

title: Cellarulo
description: An area in the Contrada Cellarulo of Benevento that is designated as an archaeological area with evidence for the later phases of ancient Benevento's history.

title: Shrine of Sabazius
description: The Shrine of Sabazius was installed in part of a horreum (V, XII, 2) that was initially built ca. 120-125 CE. The Sabazius shrine likely dates to the early third century. Dante Vaglieri excavated the shrine in 1909.

title: Baths of the Philosopher
description: The so-called "Baths of the Philosopher" or "Terme del Filosofo" in region V of the ancient city of Ostia take their modern sobriquet from a bust of Plotinus dating to the middle of the third century CE.

title: Domus, M. Tullius Cicero
description: The house of the Roman statesman and orator M. Tullius Cicero was located on the north-eastern corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome.

title: Poikile Petra
description: Poikile Petra is the name of a road connecting Seleucia ad Calycadnum and Corycus.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 66 D4 Poikile Petra

title: Chiesa Ipogea di San Nicola
description: A poorly understood paleochristian site located on the grounds of the Inviolata park in the comune of Guidonia-Montecelio in the greater metropolitan area of Rome. The cave site may originally have functioned as a mithraeum.

title: Roman amphitheater at Thermae Himeraeae
description: Roman amphitheater at Termini Imerese was of modest size and is today poorly preserved.

title: Torre d'en Galmés
description: Torre d'en Galmés was a Talaiotic settlement of Bronze Age Minorca and was established ca. 1400 BC.

title: Stadium at Kibyra
description: The Stadium at Kibyra dates to the second and third centuries CE and could seat about 10,000 people.

title: Remoria
description: A place, perhaps legendary, connected with Remus, Romulus' twin brother. It may have been located five miles downstream from the Palatine Hill.

title: Hellenopolis
description: Likely founded by Attalos II, Hellenopolis was initially populated by an amalgamation of citizens from several nearby Greek cities, and was located somewhere near the Mysia-Bithynia border.

title: Ploutonion at Hierapolis
description: The Ploutonion at Hierapolis is a walled sanctuary dedicated to Pluto and Kore.

title: Cetona
description: The present town of Cetona grew around the rocca (fortress) of the tenth century A.D., although occupation at the site reaches back to the Paleolithic when a number of caves show evidence for human activity. There are also indications of an Etruscan phase of occupation.

title: Castelliere di Monte Acuto
description: A multi-period site on Monte Acuto with evidence for habitation (Late Bronze Age) and cult activities (mid-first millennium BCE).

title: Romano-British Bath House
description: A bathhouse located at Orpington, Kent was excavated between 1971 and 1975. The site flourished between ca. 270 and 400 CE. Its post-abandonment phase includes Anglo-Saxon graves of the fifth and sixth centuries.

title: Maiden Castle, Dorset
description: One of the largest and most complex Iron Age hillforts in Europe, Maiden Castle, in Dorset, was occupied from the Neolithic period through to the fourth century A.D.

title: Roman theater at Amiternum
description: The Roman theater at Amiternum could seat approximately 2,000 people. It was abandoned after the fourth century and became a necropolis.

title: Marigny à Fleurville Gallo-Roman Villa
description: Remains of a Gallo-Roman Villa at modern Château de Marigny at Fleurville, France.

title: Komninon (Macedonian tomb), Stavroupolis
description: Stavroupolis is the site of the largest Macedonian tomb known in Thrace.

title: House of Julius Polybius
description: The House of Julius Polybius (IX 13,1.3) sits on the north side of the Via dell'Abbondanza and dates from the second century BC.

title: Roman baths, Carsulae
description: Baths of the early imperial period at Carsulae.

title: Castello di Agropoli
description: A Medieval castle built atop Byzantine foundations.

title: Arch of Hadrian at Athens
description: The Arch of Hadrian is a monument in the form of a Roman triumphal arch, constructed by the citizens of Athens in AD 131 or 132 to honor the Roman emperor Hadrian.

title: Roman theater of Neapolis
description: The Roman theater of Neapolis is a structure of the first century B.C. that is built atop the pre-existing fourth century B.C. Greek theater.

title: Bouleuterion of Onchestos
description: The Bouleuterion of Onchestos has been identified adjacent to the Temple of Poseidon.

title: ager Mutycensis
description: The territory of Motyca in the Roman province of Sicilia that, according to Cicero, supported 187 farmers.

title: Kybele Sanctuary at Kapikaya
description: The Kybele Sanctuary at Kapikaya is a rock-cut sanctuary sacred to Kybele, approximately 6 km from Pergamon, and is included in the UNESCO World Heritage site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

title: Abū Fanduwā
description: Settlement inhabited in the 5th-4th milliennia BCE, located in the modern Hoseynabad-e Goruh Rural District of Iran's Kerman province.

title: Nuraghe Su Valsu
description: A Middle Bronze Age nuraghe located southwest of Florinas in Sardinia.

title: Upton-by-Chester
description: A Roman camp was identified via crop marks in 1989 and confirmed thereafter. It covers an area of approximately 1.2 hectares. The site is located in two fields to the west of the lane from Acres Lane to Upton Grange.

title: Roman theater of Philippopolis
description: The Roman theater in Plovdiv, Bulgaria.

title: Odeon of Philippopolis
description: The ancient Roman odeon in Plovdiv, Bulgaria.

description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 23 unlocated Zargidaua

title: Via Ciminia
description: The Via Ciminia was a Roman road that left the Via Cassia and continued toward the Ciminian hills. Its course likely ran from Sutrium to near Viterbo.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 42 C4 Via Ciminia

title: Odéon at Carthage
description: The theater and odéon of Roman Carthage stood in the northeast of the city, some three blocks from the cardo maximus.

title: Neolithic Settlement at Knossos
description: A neolithic settlement on a hill known today as Kephala, south of Heraklion on the island of Crete. It preceded the Bronze Age (Minoan) palace and settlement on this site.

title: Civitas Leonina
description: The Civitas Leonina or Leonine City is a portion of the city of Rome on the left bank of the river Tiber around which Pope Leo IV commissioned the construction of the Leonine Wall in the ninth century AD. This followed the Saracen sack of Rome in AD 846.

title: Qutb Minar
description: The second tallest minar (73 m) in India after Minar-E-Fateh was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak beginning in AD 1192. The monument is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Tell Um Hammad al-Gharbi
description: Archaeological site on the banks of the Zerqa River with signs of habitation in the Early Bronze Age I-II and IV. The eastern portion of the larger Tell Um Hammad site is called Um Hammad Sharqiya; the western section is Um Hammad al-Gharbi. The two may have been linked as a single village in the Early Bronze Age IV.

title: Uronarti
description: An ancient settlement located on an island in the Nile just south of the Second Cataract, now in the north of Sudan. An ancient fortress dating to the reigns of the Middle Kingdom pharaohs (19th century BC), Senusret I and Senusret III, is found there.

title: Temple of Augustus and Rome (Ankara)
description: The Temple of Augustus and Roma at Ankara likely dates ca. 20 BCE. It is also known as the "Monumentum Ancyranum", highlighting the structure's role in preserving the most complete copy of the inscription known as the "Res Gestae Divi Augusti", which was promulgated in both ancient Greek and Latin following the death of emperor Augustus in 14 CE.

title: Cadbury Camp Hill Fort
description: A 2.8 ha hill fort near Tickenham, Somerset, England, in use from the Bronze Age to the Anglo-Saxon period.

title: Church of St. George
description: One of a group of eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches located in Lalibela, a city in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia. The church likely dates to the twelfth or thirteenth century.

title: Southeastern Cluster
description: The Southeastern Cluster of rock-cut churches at Lalibela.

title: Roman theater at Antium
description: The Roman theater at Antium is most likely built in the second half of the first century.

title: Kaims Castle
description: Kaims Castle is a Roman fortlet located between the forts of Ardoch and Strageath.

title: House of the Triclinium at Italica
description: House of the Triclinium is located in the area southeast of the House of Hylas.

title: Appleby-in-Westmorland
description: A Roman signal station of the "Gask ridge" type was located 1.5 miles southeast of Appleby-in-Westmorland.

title: Corinthian League
description: The League of Corinth was a federation of Greek states that was created by Philip II of Macedon in 338–337 BC.

title: Vessagiriya
description: Vessagiriya is the site of an ancient Buddhist forest monastery in Sri Lanka. It is considered part of the ruined site of Anuradhapura. The monastery was initially built in the middle of the third century BCE and was expanded in the late fifth century CE. A Roman bronze coin, as well as punch-marked coins and/or ingots, were excavated at Vessagiriya in the first decade of the 20th century.

title: House of the Fishes
description: A domus in Ostia Antica, whose two building phases have been dated, respectively, to the middle and last quarter of the third century CE.

title: Malkata
description: Site located south of the Theban Necropolis containing a New Kingdom palace complex constructed by Amenhotep III of the 18th Dynasty.

title: Garden Houses
description: A large residential complex, built in ca. 128 CE as part of the Hadrianic remodeling of Ostia. Its central area was occupied by two blocks, each comprising four houses, surrounded by a garden furnished with six fountains.

title: Adad Gate
description: The Adad Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the western side of the inner city, directly west of the nu-x-ù quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.

title: Teatro Marittimo
description: The so-called "Maritime Theater" at the Villa of Hadrian in Tivoli is sometimes referred to as the 'island villa'. It served as a kind of inner sanctum within the larger complex of the Villa Hadriana.

title: North Palace at Babylon
description: The Neo-Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC) constructed a new royal residence for himself at Babylon. This grand palace was constructed north of the so-called “South Palace,” the traditional royal residence of the kings of Babylon. The building, which is referred to as the “new palace” (ēkallu eššu) in Achaemenid-period texts, is generally called the “North Palace,” “Nordburg,” and “New Palace.”

title: Rhagiane
description: A region of Media centring on the city of Rhagai.

title: Tell Leilan
description: Tell Leilan is situated near the Wadi Jarrah, in the Khabur River basin in Al-Hasakah Governorate, northeastern Syria. The ancient names of the site are Shekhna and Shubat-Enlil.

title: Gleieh
description: Gleieh (also Gleiʾeh, Glaiʿā) is a small site in the middle Euphrates region and was part of the kingdom of Suhu. The city, which is probably to be identified with ancient Kār-Apladad, was situated on the south bank of the Euphrates, opposite Sur Jureh (which lies on the northern bank). Like many towns and cities of the ancient kingdom of Suhu, Gleieh/Kār-Apladad is now underwater; the area was flooded after the construction of the Haditha dam.

title: Villa di Prastina Pacato
description: Villa di Prastina Pacato, a suburban villa of ancient Tusculum.

title: Vica
description: A place included on the Peutinger map.

title: Tell 'Ira
description: Tell located on the 'Ira mountain spur at the southernmost spur of the Hebron hills in the northeastern Negev. Tell 'Ira has archaeological remains from the Early Bronze Age, Iron Age, Hellenistic and Roman periods, Byzantine, and early Islamic periods.

title: Herakleion
description: An ancient sanctuary of Hercules (Melqart) that Strabo places at one end of the long island (Cotinussa) that extended south from ancient Gades. Significant landscape and coastal change have occurred since antiquity, disrupting the integrity of these islands. Nonetheless, modern scholars have consistently identified the location of the sanctuary as at or near the 17th-18th century Castillio de Sancti Petri, which today occupies a separate homonymous islet. Archaeological finds possibly associated with the sanctuary have been made in the vicinity (both terrestrial and underwater) over the years, but precise location of foundations or other identifiable architecture have remained elusive.

title: Sepolcreto Ostiense
description: The modern toponym "Sepolcreto Ostiense" refers to a portion of what was once a vast ancient necropolis in Rome, located between the Rupe di San Paolo and the bend of the Tiber River. Nearby are the remains of the church of Santa Croce.

The city had a long history, beginning in the Archaic period when Orthagorid tyrants ruled it. It flourished in later Archaic and Classical times, was a member of the Peloponnesian League, and became a center of Theban power after 371 B.C. The city was long noted for its association with fine arts and during the fourth century B.C. produced the famous sculptor Lysippos. Under Aratos, Sicyon joined the Achaean League in 251 B.C. By the time Pausanias visited the site, declining political fortunes and disastrous earthquakes had reduced it to a ruinous state.

title: Kalhu Archive 17
description: Among private houses in the north-east of the citadel, in Room 19 of House III, British excavators found forty-seven clay tablets, including two dockets, which might have been once attached to Aramaic texts written on perishable material (e.g., papyrus). This private archive belonged to the eunuch Šamaš-šarru-uṣur and a few other influential men. While most of the texts are loans of silver, corn, or birds, eleven of the texts are sale documents. There is also a list of silver and birds connected to different citizens of Kalhu.

title: Mausoleum Campo Barbarico
description: The Campo Barbarico Mausoleum is a third-century CE Roman "temple tomb" located at the fourth mile of the Via Latina. The tomb's position is immediately to the south of the archaeological area of the Tombs of the Via Latina. In 2022, additional in situ tracts of the Via Latina's pavement were excavated adjacent to the mausoleum.

title: Roman necropolis at Carmo
description: A necropolis of the Roman period wherein most tombs date between the first century BC and the second century AD.

title: Italia, Regio IX

title: Eandasaya

According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two temples in that part of Babylon.

title: Ekitušgirzal
description: The temple of the goddess Bēlet-Eanna, Ekitušgirzal (“House, Abode of Joy”), was located in the New City district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two temples in that part of Babylon.

title: Bakcheion

title: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido
description: The so-called Temple of Venus and Cupid at Rome is part of the complex of buildings associated with the Sessorian palace. The structure's modern assignation is owed to the discovery of a fragmentary statue of Sallustia Orbiana in the guise of Venus Felix. Sallustia Orbiana was the wife of Alexander Severus. The statue is now held in the Museo Pio Clementino in the Vatican Museums.

title: Terme Aquae Passeris

title: Porticus margaritaria

title: Tripodiskos
description: Now unlocated, Tripodiskos was a market center of Megara. According to Pausanias, its name is connected to the activities of Coroebus who was ordered by the Pythia of Delphi to carry the Delphic tripod and to establish a new shrine to the god at the place where it fell from his hands. title: Tretos
description: From Hesiod onward, Greek writers locate the Nemean lion in a cave or ravine in this mountain and explain the mountain's name ("perforated") from being split by the ravine. Wiseman (in PECS, whence ToposText) identifies the Tretos as "the mountain on the W side of the main road between Kleonaia-Corinthia and Argolis" and the ravine as the modern Dervenakia pass. Camp in BAtlas silently suppresses this view, and mentioning "Tretos" only in a list of "unlocated" features in the map-by-map directory where he cites only Pausanias and glosses: "Corinthia-Argolis: pass, road".

title: (As)Syria (region)

For the Assyrian kings and subsequent imperial powers of the region (as well as Biblical authors), it was confined to a more specific area along the Tigris, corresponding to what is now sometimes referred to as the "Assyrian Homeland". title: Temple of Aphrodite on the Acrocorinth
description: A temple to Aphrodite on the Acrocorinth likely constructed in the 5th century BCE. According to Plutarch, the women of Corinth prayed to the statue of the armed Aphrodite to instil the 'eros' of battle in their men during the Greco-Persian war. The armed Aphrodite was a significant icon and motif of the Acrocorinthian temple, that continued after the destruction of Corinth by the Romans in 146 BCE. The temple is also famous for supposed sacred prostitution, as described by Strabo, but these claims are unverified.

title: Hermes and Aphrodite Sanctuary
description: This large, open-air sanctuary near Syme Viannou in southern Crete was in use from 2000 BCE until at least the sixth century CE. It attracted pilgrims who are assumed to have camped at the site, which is far from any contemporary settlement. Monumental construction began in the early second millennium BCE and multiple phases and changes are evident, including the construction of Christian chapels in late antiquity. title: Varnava Tower
description: A square, stone tower known today as Varnava Tower (Ο πύργος του Βαρνάβα), located outside the modern village of Varnava in Greece.

title: Sounion (Attica: settlement and deme)
description: The fortified port settlement at Sounion, a coastal deme of Leontis, served the Athenian grain ships originating in Euboea and was the site of the sanctuary of Poseidon, among others.

title: Zea Limen

provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B3 Zea Limen

title: Thria
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Thria

title: Salamis (settlement)
description: The ancient city of Salamis was located on the Saronic island of the same name, overlooking the modern Ampelaki Bay to the east. The site was likely largely in the area now covered by the modern city of Ambelaki/Ampelaki.

title: Tetrakomoi
description: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: N and E Peiraieus.

title: Zoster Pr.
description: A peninsula at modern Vouliagmeni in Attica, in myth the location where Leto loosened her girdle before giving birth to Artemis and Apollo.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 C3 Zoster Pr.

title: Tetrapolis
description: A district of northeastern Attica that included the cities of Marathon, Probalinthus, Tricorythus, and Oenoe.

title: Salamis (island)
description: Salamis is the largest island of the Saronic Gulf.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 A3 Salamis Ins.

title: Thriasion Lager
description: The Thriasion Lager was a fortified camp in ancient Attica located 3 km. west of the so-called Dema Wall.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B2 Thriasion Lager

title: Zeus Ombrios, T.
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Zeus Ombrios, T.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B2 Zeus Ombrios, T.

title: Basilica di Santa Restituta
description: The Basilica of Santa Restituta is a Christian church in Naples, Italy. It is considered the oldest Christian basilica in the city. Tradition assigns its foundation to Constantine I, and the Liber Pontificalis identifies him as patron in a passage from the life of Pope Sylvester I. The Christian church may have occupied a location that was formerly home to a temple of Apollo.

title: Nuraghe Arrubiu
description: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic site (ca. 1500 BC) near Cagliari, Sardinia.

title: Lothal
description: Lothal is among the southernmost cities of the ancient Indus Valley civilisation. The site is located in India, specifically in the Bhal region of the Indian state of Gujarat. The settlement dates ca. 2300 BCE.

title: Untitled
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Eleusis from NE)

title: Untitled
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C2 unnamed aqueduct (Athens from N)
