description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C2 unnamed aqueduct (Peiraeus from NE)

title: Hospitalet Vell
description: A prehistoric settlement of Mallorca with two phases: a Pre-Talayotic period (ca. 1700/1600 to 1200/1100 BCE) and a Talayotic phase (ca. 1100 to 123 BCE). There is also some evidence of Punic influence.

title: Hedemünden
description: An early Imperial fort located on the river Werra.

title: Santa Maria Nova
description: A multi-period site with medieval and modern remains atop Roman levels, including a medieval farmhouse built atop a Roman cistern. Excavations revealed multi-phase evidence, including a bath building decorated with mosaics. The structures may have been related to the nearby Villa dei Quintilli.

title: Mausoleum of Gallienus
description: A mausoleum on the Via Appia that has been identified conventionally as that of the emperor Gallienus.

title: Assur Archive 29
description: In the grave chamber and some other areas of House 33 (dB5IV), above the Middle Assyrian palace terrace, researchers found a small archive of 8 clay tablets. The archive contains purchase documents, a document concerning the division of inheritance, a receipt of payment, a list, and a letter of complaint.

title: Ponte di Annibale
description: An arched Roman bridge across the Titerno near Cerreto Sannita in Campania.

title: Mons Faliscorum
description: Mons Faliscorum (modern Montefiascone) originally a Faliscan settlement, came later to be controlled by the Etruscans.

title: Mar Elian
description: The beginnings of the early Christian monastery of Saint Elian at Al-Qaryatayn, Syria, are linked with the saint Julian of Emesa. The Medieval iteration of the monastery was badly damaged - or perhaps nearly destroyed - by Islamic State terrorists in 2015.

title: Via Flaminia militare
description: The Via Flaminia Militare, or Via Flaminia Minor, was a road constructed by Gaius Flaminius in 187 BCE that connected Arretium and Bononia.

title: Via Ardeatina
description: The Via Ardeatina connected Rome and Ardea.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 43 C2 Via Ardeatina

title: Crac des Chevaliers
description: An ancient castle, located in modern Syria. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006 as part of the "Crac des Chevaliers and Qal’at Salah El-Din" listing.

title: Qalb Lozé
description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of an ancient basilica. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

title: Deirouné
description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of a monastic chapel. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

title: Kafr Aqareb
description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of Roman praetorium, a temple and grottoes for pagan worship, a Byzantine basilica, and a large communal reservoir. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

title: Galatas
description: A Minoan palatial center on Crete, dated ca. 1700-1600 BC, that was discovered in the 1990s.

title: Lantonside
description: A Roman fortlet of Antonine period in Scotland.

title: Narekavank
description: Narekavank, or Narek Monastery, was a tenth-century Armenian monastery near the southern shore of Lake Van. It was a major monastic center, and the mystical poet Grigor Narekatsi (951-1003) studied and resided there. The monastery was abandoned and demolished in the 20th century.

title: Fort Shalmaneser
description: The ninth-century-BC Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858–824 BC) constructed an impressive palatial complex in the southeastern corner of the city Kalhu (biblical Calah). This armory, which the seventh-century-BC ruler Esarhaddon (r. 680–669 BC) referred to as an ēkal māšarti (‘review palace’), was completed ca. 846 BC. Fort Shalmaneser, the name of building dubbed by its excavators, remained in use until the very end of the Assyrian Empire (612 BC), although its importance was significantly diminished after the Assyrian court moved away from Kalhu at the end of the eighth century BC, first to Dūr-Šarrukīn and then to Nineveh.

title: Mugharet Abu Halimeh
description: Cave tomb near the modern village of Silat aḑ-Ḑahr containing burials from the Roman and Byzantine periods (1st-early 7th century CE). The cave is named after the Abu Halimeh family, which owned the land on which the cave is located at the time of its excavation in 1949.

title: Governor's Palace at Kalhu
description: This beautifully-decorated Assyrian palace is located just north of the Nabû temple Ezida, in the southeast quarter of the citadel of Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). The building likely served as the office and/or residence of several important individuals in the administration of the Assyrian Empire, probably including the governor of Kalhu. Numerous cuneiform tablets were discovered in three rooms north of the central courtyard. Because many of those Akkadian texts relate to the activities of several governors, British excavators in the 1950s dubbed the building the "Governor's Palace."

title: Domus Lucina
description: The Domus Lucina was located on the Via Lata, which is the site where a certain widowed matrona named Lucina harbored Marcellus I and then established a church in his name.

title: Mousa
description: Mousa is an island in Shetland, Scotland.

title: Sitagroi
description: Sitagroi is the location of an important archaeological site from the late Neolithic period and early Bronze Age.

title: Grand mausolée des Flavii
description: A mausoleum near Cillium dates to the second century CE. Tiberius Flavius Secundus built the family tomb, dedicating it to his father, and inscribing two poetic texts totaling some 110 lines on its facade. Located in what is now Kasserine, Tunisia.

title: Palace G at Ebla
description: Palace at Ebla dated to the early Bronze Age (24th century BCE), built atop the remains of an older palace (designated G2). Palace G, destroyed around 2300 BCE, contained an extensive archive of clay tablets.

title: Mausoleum of Bibi Maryam at Qalhat
description: The Mausoleum of Bibi Maryam at Qalhat was built for Baha al-Din Ayaz, the successor of Mahmud b. Ahmad al-Qusi al-Qalhati, the founder of the Hormuz empire which flourished from the eighth to the fourteenth century.

title: Bozköy-Hanaytepe
description: A settlement mound and archaeological site located in the Troad containing evidence of habitation from the Chalcolithic through the Late Bronze Ages.

title: Philippeion
description: The Philippeion is a tholos at Olympia constructed to celebrate Philip II's victory at Chaeonea in 338 BCE and completed by Alexander the Great.

title: Sanctuary of Artemis at Avlonas
description: A sanctuary possibly sacred to Artemis on the island of Lemnos.

title: Veranes
description: A Roman villa.

title: Tell Ischali
description: Tell Ishchali is an archaeological site in Iraq's Diyala province. Its main floruit in antiquity was from ca. 2700–1800 BC, primarily Dynastic through the Isin–Larsa period. The site was part of the city-state of Eshnunna.

title: Kalo Pegadi (bridge)
description: On Hiera Hodos at Kopros.

title: Theater at Leuke
description: The theater is located at the north-east end of Kouphonesi. It was a stone-built building that could accommodated ca. 1000 spectators.

title: Aedes Ceres Liber Liberaque
description: The Temple of Ceres, located on the slope of the Aventine Hill in Rome, was originally dedicated by Sp. Cassius in 494/3 B.C.
names_romanized: Temple of Ceres Liber and Libera
names_attested_other: Temple of Ceres Liber and Libera@en

title: Band-e Kaisar
description: A third century AD Roman bridge located near Shushtar, Iran.

title: Cave of Anigrid Nymphs
description: A healing sanctuary connected with the river nymphs of the river Anigros. The cave is in proximity to the thermal springs of Lake Kaiafas.

title: Kaneš
description: Kaneš or Kanesh (Hittite: Neša) is located adjacent to modern Kültepe, thus at times the site is referred to as Kültepe Kaneš. The site was one of continuous occupation from the Chalcolithic period to the time of the Roman empire, although its cultural zenith was as a major Hittite site that was the site of a large merchant quarter (kârum) of the Old Assyrian kingdom (ca. twentieth to sixteenth centuries BC).

title: Guadalimar
description: The River Guadalimar is a right-bank tributary of the Guadalquivir.

title: Visigothic necropolis, Duratón
description: A Visigothic necropolis at Duratón, Spain, that was discovered in 1929.

title: Temple of Thelsae
description: A well-preserved Roman period temple located in modern Dmeir, Syria. The sanctuary was later converted into a fortification.

title: Ponte di Annibale - Sant'Angelo
description: A Roman bridge known by a variety of local toponyms that crosses the Savuto river. It is located in the modern Italian municipality of Altilia, Calabria.

title: Matarrah
description: Hilltop settlement in northern Iraq representing one of the oldest villages of the Near East. Archaeological evidence shows that this was an early location of agricultural practices.

title: Sîn-Šamaš Temple
description: One of the temples in the citadel of Nineveh that was dedicated to the moon-god Sîn and the sun-god Šamaš. Its Sumerian ceremonial name is not preserved in extant cuneiform sources and its exact location remains unknown. The temple is generally believed to have been east of the temples of Ištar (Emašmaš) and Nabû (Ezida) and south of the North Palace (palace of Ashurbanipal).
names_romanized: bīt Sîn Ningal Šamaš u Aya|Sîn-Šamaš Temple

title: Possible heroön (Salamis)
description: A seven-room building was brought to light by underwater archaeological research in Salamis. The architectural remains may be those of a hero shrine (heroön) connected with the Greek hero Ajax.

title: Saint-Aunès milestone
description: A Roman milestone of the Via Aurelia.

title: Oppidum du Castellan
description: A Gallic oppidum occupied from the sixth century B.C.

title: Rota
description: What would become Medieval Rota was once a pagus of Etruscan Caere. Writing in PECS, Mario Torelli describes this an an important Archaic center in the area of Tolfa.

title: Yalvac Theatre - Antioch Pisidia
description: The theater at Pisidian Antioch was perhaps founded in the first century BCE.

title: Augusteum, Antioch in Pisidia
description: The Augusteum, or Sebasteion, at Antioch in Pisidia was a monumental architectural complex dedicated to the Roman Imperial cult. Its archaeological remains were first excavated in 1913. Approximately 60 fragments of the Res Gestae Divi Augusti were discovered at the site.

title: Roman amphitheater at Trier
description: The Roman amphitheater at Trier dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius and was renovated under Constantius Chlorus. The arena measures ca. 71 x 47.5 meters.
names_romanized: Amphitheatre in Trier|Das Amphitheater in Trier
names_attested_other: Amphitheatre in Trier@en|Das Amphitheater in Trier@de

title: Neuri
description: A tribe whose territory was located on the Hypanis to the west of the Borysthenes.

title: Balsignano
description: A fortified Medieval site located in Puglia.

title: Theater of Zea
description: Visible remains of a Hellenistic theater located to the west of the Zea Harbor in Piraeus, dating ca. 200 B.C.

title: Böyük Kəsik
description: Chalcolithic settlement in modern Azerbaijan. The settlement was oval shaped and was 1.2 hectares in area, but the top layers were destroyed and the lower layers are not visible due to ongoing agriculture on the site.

title: Brihadishwara Temple
description: 11th century Hndu temple Tanjuvar dedicated to Shiva with smaller shrines around it.

title: Tell Karanovo
description: Neolithic settlement in the Azmak River Valley inhabited from the 7th-2nd millennia BCE. The hilltop settlement is the type site of the Karanovo culture.

title: Dugali Alti
description: Dugali Alti or Dugali Alti di Ostiano is an archaeological site located near Ostiano in Cremona, Italy, that has provided evidence of agricultural practices in the Neolithic period of northern Italy.

title: Nuraghe Palmavera
description: A site near Alghero, Sardinia, belonging to the first nuragic phase (fifteenth and fourteenth centuries BC).

title: Samian Poseidon Sanctuary (Triphylia)
description: A cult place of Samian Poseidon erected during the Archaic period and located near Kleidi/Kato Samikon, Ileia, Greece.

title: Kleidí
description: An archaeological site located on a coastal hill near Samikon, Kleidi presents evidence for both prehistoric settlement and a cemetery.

title: Blenheim Roman villa
description: A Roman villa partially excavated in 1985 with pottery dating from the third and fourth centuries CE near Woodstock, Oxfordshire, United Kingdom.

title: Pellana (Mycenaean cemetery)
description: Mycenaean chamber tombs located to the north of Pellana in Laconia.

title: Poggino necropolis
description: An Etruscan necropolis in Chianti in use between the seventh and fifth centuries BC.

title: Villa del Vergigno, Montelupo Fiorentino
description: A large villa rustica inhabited from ca. 100 B.C. to A.D. 500, located near Montelupo Fiorentino in the mid-Arno Valley of northern Tuscany, approximately twenty km west of Florence.

title: Marina di Palo Roman villa
description: An Imperial maritime villa located in Ladispoli, Italy.

title: Temple of Hera, Olympia
description: The Temple of Hera at Olympia, also known as the Heraion, is a peripteral temple located in the northwest corner of the Altis precinct, dedicated to Hera. Built ca. 600-590 B.C., the Heraion is the oldest temple at Olympia and one of the earliest known examples of the Doric order in Greece.

title: Roman amphitheater of Thyna
description: A Roman amphitheater located at Thaenea, a Roman station in the province of Africa Proconsularis.

title: Temple of the Severan family
description: Near a bath complex built under Commodus, a Severan complex that included a plaza, porticoes, and a temple dedicated to the Severan family was added.

title: Sceilg Mhichíl
description: A monastic complex on Skellig Michael established in the seventh century A.D. and enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

title: Colombarone
description: An archaeological site that preserves remains of a Late Roman settlement along the Via Flaminia.

title: Sant'Ilario
description: A paleochristian site located at the thirtieth mile of the ancient via Labicana, near to the ancient road station 'ad Bivium'.

title: Tre Ponti necropolis
description: A necropolis along the Via Amerina, likely in use from the third century BC until the third century AD.

title: Villa di Teodorico
description: A palatial Roman villa and bath complex that has been connected with Theodoric the Great, with twentieth century interpretations labeling it as Theodoric's "hunting lodge". More recent excavations have uncovered evidence for earlier building phases, dating from the first century B.C. through the third century A.D.

title: Montefortini
description: A monumental Etruscan tumulus that covers two chamber tombs that were looted in antiquity but that likely dated to the seventh and sixth centuries B.C.

title: Tomba di Boschetti
description: An archaic Etruscan tumulus located near Comeana, Italy.

title: Western gate of Serdica
description: Fortification at the western edge of the settlement of Serdica, constructed in the 2nd century CE and disused by the end of the 6th century CE. The site was excavated in 2011-2013 and is now an archaeological park.

title: House of Plotilla
description: The House of Plotilla, also known as Casa di Apollo e Coronide, was excavated in 1815 and again in 1839. It lies in Regio VIII of Pompeii.

title: Basílica de Santa Eulalia
description: The Basílica de Santa Eulalia is a paleochristian site that is included as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida". The early Christian features were superimposed upon previous, preexisting Roman features.

title: Darb Qirmiz
description: Darb Qirmiz is a residential neighborhood in the tenth-century Fatimid quarter of Cairo, Egypt, with the oldest remaining monuments dating from the fourteenth century.

title: Large Temple at Sikait
description: A large rock-cut temple at Sikait in Egypt's Eastern desert.

title: Abū Ṣalābīḫ
description: A place from the TAVO Index

title: Cassiterides
description: An unlocatable group of islands somewhere off the Atlantic European coast, said by ancient authors to be a source of tin. This name may constitute an early, vague generalization concerning multiple islands and coastal areas of Gaul and Britain.

title: Acquedotto dei Sette Bassi
description: A Roman aqueduct supplying the Villa dei Sette Bassi.

title: Diyālā
description: A place from the TAVO Index

title: Tuttul
description: Tuttul was a Bronze Age city that is associated with the archaeological site of Tell Bi'a located in the Raqqa Governorate of northern Syria. The tell lies near the confluence of the Balikh and Euphrates rivers.

title: Shir as-Sanam Inscription
description: A Neo-Babylonian rock relief of Nebuchadnezzar II was found in the area of the modern city Qubbayat, close to the Wadi Oustane and the Jebel Akroum. The monument at Shir as-Sanam is about 16 Km from Qubbayat, on the road to Chambouq and Hermel. It is about located ca. 120 meters from the road, on the western side, 15 m. above the ground.

title: Schola Praeconum
description: The so-called Schola Praeconum is located at the foot of the Palatine Hill near the church of S. Anastasia. A black-and-white floor mosaic discovered during excavations depicts public heralds known as praecones, thus the name of the site.

title: Palaestra at Olympia
description: Palaestra in the sanctuary of Zeus at Olympia

title: Old Town of Ghadamès
description: The Old Town of Ghadamès was inscribed in 1986 as a UNESCO World Heritage site, but was de-populated throughout the 1990s. It is now listed on the List of World Heritage in Danger (2016).

title: Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus
description: The Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus is a Roman-period tomb, possibly of tholos typology, located in the Porta Nocera necropolis of Pompeii.

description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 A2 unnamed fort (W Eleusis)

title: Lykabettos (mountain)
description: Lykabettos is a limestone hill in Athens, Greece.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B3 Lykabettos M.

title: Akte Pr.
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Akte Pr.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B3 Akte Pr.

title: Ardettos
description: A site to the southeast of Athens, where jurors swore their oath, named for a hero Ardettes.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B3 Ardettos M.

title: Melite
description: Melite was a deme of ancient Attica. It was located in the urban center of Athens and included both the Agora and the Pnyx. It belonged to the tribe of Kekropis.

title: Kydathenaion
description: Kydathenaion was the third largest deme of Attica, with only Acharnae and Aphidna being larger. It was located within the city walls of Athens and perhaps included the Acropolis and the Areopagus as well.

title: Skambonidai
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Skambonidai

title: Kolonos Hippios
description: Pausanias states that the Kolonos Hippios is a hill that marks the first point that Oedipus reached in Attica. It was a sacred area with rites devoted to both Poseidon and Athena, as well as a hero shrine sacred to Peirithous and Theseus, Oedipus and Adrastus. Antigonus destroyed the shrine of Poseidon.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B2 Kolonos Hippios

title: Eetioneia Pr.
description: A fortified promontory located on the western side of the main port of Piraeus.
provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 59 B3 Eetioneia Pr.

title: Kollytos
description: An Attic asty deme belonging to the Aegeis phyle.

title: Boviolles
description: Gallo-Roman hilltop settlement

title: Theater of Chersonesos
description: A Hellenistic theater located in the ancient Greek colony of Tauric Chersonesos. Built in the 4th or 3rd century BC, it remained in use through the Roman period. It is one of the few surviving examples of Greek theater architecture in the northern Black Sea region.

title: South-Western Baths
description: A bath complex at Herculaneum that was discovered in the excavations of the so-called "Insula Occidentalis". It was not in use as a bath at the time of the 79 CE eruption as it had been repurposed as a ship-shed.

title: Roman Baths of Como
description: The Roman Baths of Como were in use from the later first century until the third century CE.

title: Roman baths, Spoleto
description: Roman baths located at Spoletium.

title: Ilıca (Ayas: cemetery)
description: Cemetery site northwest of Ankara containing burials dated to the Hittite period (16th century BCE). The modern neighborhood of Ilıca is in the Ayas district of Turkey's Ankara province.

title: Shrine of Strenia
description: The Shrine of Strenia was located in the valley of the Colosseum and is mentioned as the starting point of the Sacra Via.

title: Peschiera necropolis
description: An Etruscan necropolis at Tuscania in use from the seventh until the first century B.C.

title: Esparragalejo dam
description: Dating to the first century AD, the Esparragalejo dam is the earliest known multiple arch buttress dam.

title: Krasnyĭ mai͡ak
description: Late Scythian burial site on the Lower Dnieper River containing burials dated to the 3rd century BCE-2nd century CE.

title: Stepushka
description: Burial site in the Altai region dated to the Syanbi-Zhouzhan period (4th-5th century CE).

title: Library of Pantainos
description: The modern name for a library built on the southeast corner of the Agora in Athens by Flavius Pantainos ca. 97-102 AD. It was demolished to make way for the Post-Herulian Wall in the late third century AD.

title: Themakos
description: Themakos was an Attic deme of the Erechtheid tribe.

title: Kyrteidai
description: Now unlocated, Kyrteidai was an Attic deme belonging to the phyle Akamantis.

title: Tripyrgia
description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 unlocated Tripyrgia

description: Eitea was a deme of the tribe Akamantis, located in Attica. It is attested by literary and documentary sources, but its precise location cannot be determined today

title: Hypereia (spring)
description: Strabo locates a Hypereia krēnē, mentioned in the Iliad's "Catalog of Ships", at Pherai in Thessaly (modern Velestino) and geographically criticizes its assignment by Homer to the contingent led by Eurypylos. Without comment, Pliny places "fons Hyperia" immediately before "oppida Pherae" in a list of places in Thessaly (E. Kirsten in RE accepts this as a reference to the spring at Pherai, but BAtlDir lists it as an "unlocated spring in Thessaly"). Archaeological work confirms a perennial spring at Velestino was a locus of settlement activity from the Neolithic period onwards, and a structure monumentalizing the spring was built and modified during the Classical and Hellenistic periods.

title: Porta Fontinalis
description: No longer extant, the Porta Fontinalis is only known via textual and epigraphic references. Presumed to be a gate of the Servian Wall, the Porta Fontinalis lay in the Campus Martius, west of the via Lata. It may have been the original point of issuance for the Republican roads known as the Via Flaminia and the Via Salaria.

title: Porta Flaminia

title: Sanctuary of Demeter (Knossos)
description: The sanctuary sacred to Demeter is located on the Gypsadhes hill, just south of the Minoan 'palace' complex. On this hill, D.G. Hogarth excavated a series of Minoan houses beginning in 1900. Within this area, a first-millennium BCE sanctuary would develop. Excavation reports note the comingling of Minoan remains and Hellenistic deposits. The Classical sanctuary was suspected in 1927 on the basis of sporadic finds, but significant excavations did not begin until 1957.

title: Nabulu

title: Temple of Artemis Orthasia
description: Remains of a sanctuary located on Mt. Kotilon northwest of the Bassai temple.

title: Kamouh el Hermel
description: An ancient pyramidal monument located 6 km south of Hermel in the Baalbek-Hermel Governorate, Lebanon. The monument likely dates to the second century BCE.

title: Castello Savelli Torlonia
description: A castle at Palombara Sabina that originates in the eleventh century.

title: Pyramid of Senusret II
description: Senusret II was a pharaoh of the Twelfth dynasty of ancient Egypt.

title: Mogao Caves
description: Buddhist cave monastery complex in the cliffs above the Dachuan River near the Dunhaung Oasis, constructed in 366 CE and in use until the 14th Century CE. The caves contain thousands of murals and painted sculptures, and thousands of manuscripts in Chinese, Tibetan, Uyghur, Sogdian, Sanskrit, and Khotanese were stored in the so-called "Library Cave." The Mogao Caves were added to UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1987.

title: Temple of Anu and Adad at Assur
description: A distinctive feature of the city of Assur is the double-temple of the gods Anu and Adad. This building, together with its twin ziggurats, was constructed no later than the Middle Assyrian period; it underwent a major rebuilding in the reign of Tiglath-pileser I (1114–1076 BC). The existence of an (unnamed) Adad temple at Assur, however, is known from inscriptions of the Old Assyrian rulers Erišum I and Ikūnum. The various parts of this axisymmetric, double-temple was given Sumerian names: Anu’s temple and ziggurat were called Ešaan and Emelamanna; and Adad’s temple and ziggurat went by the names Ešuddegeštuku and Egišlamšaršar.

title: Adilcevaz
description: Medieval castle of the town Adilcevaz on the shore of Lake Van where Urartian inscriptions have been found. Not to be confused with Kef Kalesi which is located further north and outside of Adilcevaz.

title: Tall Abū al-Dhahab
description: Archaeological site in the marches of Dhi Qar where Iraqi excavations have revealed secular and religious buildings belonging to the First Sealand Dynasty 1740–1374 BCE including a number of objects bearing cuneiform inscriptions.

title: Kephalos Island Settlement
description: On the small island of modern Kephalos in the Ambracian Gulf, archaeologists discovered a settlement, a pair of Christian basilicas, and other associated structures and small finds. The site may have begun as a refuge settlement in the late fifth / early sixth century CE and seems to have continued in use, possibly with a late monastic function, into the 10th century.

title: Mytikas Valley Dam
description: An ancient dam, subsequently reused, repaired, and adapted into modern times, in the Glosses pass east of Alyzeia (modern Kalima) and just below the later site of the Byzantine fortress of Varnako/Barnako. Remains of aqueduct and mill fittings of various dates have been noted; the dam and its reservoir are presumed to have been created originally (perhaps in Classical or Hellenistic times) to supply some portion of Alyzeia or its chora.

title: Tomb of C. Veranius Rufus
description: The tomb of the freedman of Caius Veranius Rufus and freedman Verania Clara in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

title: Domus of Vespasia Polla
description: A Roman domus traditionally associated with Vespasia Polla, mother of the emperor Vespasian.

title: Tell Umm al-Aqarib
description: Tell Umm al-Aqarib is the site of an ancient Sumerian city-state ca. 2300 - 2000 BCE of unknown identification.

title: Roman amphitheater at Libarna
description: The remains of the Roman amphitheater at Libarna are located in Serravalle Scrivia, Italy.

title: Roman Villa La Grottaccia
description: The remains of a Roman villa (first to fourth centuries CE) at Ladispoli. The surviving cryptoporticus gives the site its name.

title: Castle of Astypalaia
description: Remains of a Venetian castle atop the former ancient citadel of Astypalaia.

title: Askut
description: Ancient Egyptian island fortress on the Nile in the Middle Kingdom, now submerged.

title: Ponte Corvo
description: A Roman segmental arch bridge across the Bacchiglione river in Padua, Italy.

title: Tell 'Ali
description: A small site on the left bank of the Lower Zab where an archive of ca. twenty-five Middle Assyrian texts was discovered. The town was situated more or less where travellers from Aššur to the cities Nuzi and Arrapha would have crossed the Lower Zab. Tell 'Ali is identified with ancient Atmannu.

title: Tell Bazmusian
description: A site on the right bank of the Lower Zab that was excavated by Iraqi archaeologists in 1956–58. Tell Bazmusian, whose ancient name is not known, is one of the largest archaeological sites in the Ranya Plain (Sulaymaniyah Governorate, Iraq). The city was occupied from the sixth millennium BCE to the ninth century CE. A small group of Middle Assyrian tablets were discovered in a pit outside the city’s temple. Tell Bazmusian is now submerged under Lake Dukan.

title: Ager Faliscus (region)
description: The territory of the Faliscans that lay between areas where Etruscan, Latin, and Sabellic languages were spoken. The geographic limits of this territory on the right bank of the Tiber River stretch from Grotta Porciosa in the north to Capena in the south.

title: Lago dell'Accesa (lake)
description: Lago dell'Accesa is a lake located in the Colline Metallifere.

title: Campus Lanatarius
description: An area of Rome that is mentioned only in the Regionary Catalogue for Regio XII. This area was likely located between the Baths of Caracalla and the present location of the church of S. Saba.

description: Tap o' Noth hill fort is located in Aberdeenshire, Scotland; a well preserved vitrified wall survives at the site.

title: Chora of Amorgos (settlement)

title: Cheddar Gorge
description: The Cheddar Gorge is a limestone gorge in the Mendip Hills, near Somerset, England. The gorge and its many caves are the site of human activity dating back to the Upper Paleolithic.

title: Char Bakr
description: Necropolis of the Jūybāri shaikhs located approximately 5 km west of Bukhara. The complex was constructed during the 16th century around the tomb of the scholar Emām Abu Bakr Saʿd.

title: Ash Altar of Zeus Lykaios

title: Termas Menores de Mura

title: Phocian Wall
description: Herodotus describes the so-called Phocian Wall at Thermopylae as the most significant element of the built fortifications at the pass.

title: Aurelian Walls
description: The Aurelian Walls of Rome began as a fortification system built by Aurelian and Probus between 271 and 275. They enclose an area of approximately 1,400 hectares.

title: Giuggianello

title: Porta Ostiensis
description: The Porta Ostiensis, now known as the Porta San Paolo, is a gate in Rome's Aurelian Wall from which the Via Ostiensis issues.

title: Sororium Tigillum
description: Sororium Tigillum describes a wooden beam that stretched across a branch of the Sacra Via that climbed the Oppian Hill near the Compitum Acilii. The monument was flanked by altars of Iuno Sororia and Iuno Curiatius. It is an ancient monument about which there are many stories, the primary one being a link to the Horatii and Curiatii and Publius Horatius' slaying of his own sister.

title: Colossus Neronis
description: The "Colossus Neronis" or "Colossal Statue of Nero" was a monumental bronze statue of the first-century CE emperor reportedly created by Zenodorus. The statue was originally an element of the sprawling Domus Aurea of Nero but the monument endured long after Nero's reign. The statue's original position likely marked the summit of the Velian Hill. The Flavians refashioned the statue to resemble Sol and Hadrian relocated the statue nearer the Flavian amphitheater as part of the work to create the Temple of Venus and Roma.

title: Sanctuary of Zeus Aphesios (Megarid)
description: Pausanias mentions the Sanctuary of Zeus Aphesios as being located atop a mountain. The site was excavated ca. 1890 and has views over the Saronic Gulf.

title: Derveni tombs

title: Roman amphitheater of Asisium
description: In the Porta Perlici of Assisi are the remains of a first century A.D. Roman amphitheater.

title: Tell Kannâs
description: Settlement site on the Euphrates river with evidence of habitation from the 9th millennium BCE. The site declined under the Sumerians, was revived to be an important defensive location for the Akkadians, and continued to be inhabited until the 12th century BCE. The site was flooded by the creation of Lake Assad in 1974.

title: Al-Sabaa wa Arbain

title: Simoeis (river)
description: An intermittent stream attested in the Troad whose plain features as the scene of battles in Homer's account of the Trojan war. After Pliny, RE and BAtlas make the Simoeis a late, right tributary of the Xanthos. New Pauly asserts it was a tributary of the Scamander. The topography of the Scamander/Xanthos delta has changed significantly throughout antiquity and up to today by virtue of both natural processes and modern agricultural and hydraulic engineering. Modern commentators agree in identifying it with the modern Dümruk Su (i.e., Dümrek Çayı), despite the varying views of its ultimate confluence.

title: Pergamum
description: An important ancient settlement, located at modern Bergama in Turkey. It was first described in Xenophon's Anabasis and was later used as a treasury under Lysimachus. Pergamum became the administrative capital and principal city of the Attalid kingdom and dynasty (282-133 BCE) and was briefly the first capital of the Roman province of Asia. It later was a seat of a Christian bishopric and is listed in Revelation as one of the seven churches of Asia. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 under "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

title: Skepsis
description: An ancient settlement in the upper watershed of the Skamander (modern Karamenderes) river, located at and around the modern village of Kurşunlu in Turkey's Bayramiç (Çanakkale province). Significant archaeological remains, including a probable temple, on the dome-shaped hill immediately west of the modern village were reported in the 19th century, but these are no longer evident, the site having been quarried for construction in the village and in Bayramiç. Rescue excavations between the hill and the river revealed Roman and Byzantine-era structures, including a bath complex, in the late 20th century, prior to the filling of the reservoir created by the Bayramiç dam.

title: Razliq
description: Razliq is a village situated ca. 13 km north of the city Sarāb in Eastern Azerbaijan (Iran). Here a rock inscription of the Urartian king Argišti II, son of Rusa (end of 8th / first half of 7th century BCE), has been found which reports military campaigns of Argišti II to this region. As well as the rock inscription of Nashteban (CTU A 11-5) it is situated on the southern slope of the Sabalān Mountains at an altitude of 4810 m. Although the inscription reports the building of a fortress named ‘stronghold of Argišti’ no such archaeological remains have been discovered so far. Together with the rock inscriptions found in Nashteban (CTU A 11-5) and Shisheh (CTU A 11-6) the rock inscription found near Razliq is one of the Urartian inscriptions found furthest to the east.

title: Alonianum
description: Alonianum was a place in Africa that is included on the Peutinger map. It is likely a road station positioned along the way from Thelepte to Tacapae via the palus Tritonis.

title: Pī-Kasî
description: Site for the city of Pikasi dating back to the Old Babylonian period. A large number of cuneiform tablets were discovered there during excavations around year 2000.

title: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
description: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World identified by Hellenistic authors, and they may well have been historical; however, their location in the city of Babylon is unclear, as there is no definitive archaeological evidence or Babylonian texts mentioning the gardens. Both ancient and modern commentators have conflated this reported "paradeisos" with various other monuments, both real and imagined.

title: Via Claudia Valeria
description: A portion of the Via Valeria connecting Aternum and Corfinium. A Claudian milestone (CIL 9.5973) records the construction taking place in AD 48/9 and that the road ran from Cerfennia to the mouth of the Aternus river (modern Pescara).

title: Acropolis of Selinus
description: The fortified Acropolis of Selinus occupies a limestone plateau. It was planned following the Hippodamian fashion and it is most noted for the numerous Doric temples that occupied its sacred precincts.

title: Priddy
description: A Roman building located approximately 270 meters north and east of Priddy Church. The site, excavated in 1964, has been interpreted as being part of a small villa site.

title: Vicus Sulpicius
description: A street in ancient Rome that is mentioned on the so-called Capitoline Base (CIL 6, 975).

title: Gallo-Roman Amphitheater of Agen

title: Acquapendente

title: Gövelek
description: Gövelek is a village situated 27 km to the east of Van in the southeast of Turkey. Here the upper part of a stela with an inscription of Rusa, son of Erimena (presumably last quarter of 8th century BCE) was found. It reports his military success and describes deportations from the city Ṭušpa, the building of the city Rusaḫinili, and the creation of an artificial lake called "Lake of Rusa". The lake was supposed to ensure the water supply for the capital Ṭušpa (modern Van Kalesi), a function it still performs today. The lower part of the stela has been found at the shore of the lake.

title: Thermae Helenianae
description: The Thermae Helenianae or Thermae Helenae was a thermal complex located in the Horti Spei Veteris, also referred to as the Horti Variani. The baths were situated near the arcus Neroniani adjacent to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. As Helena, mother of Constantine I, restored them following a fire in 323-326, they are named for her.

title: Tell Ras Budran
